summary:
The signal today is thin on volume but loud on direction: every rating tier (R1-R4) went 1-0 across all six categories in the last 14 days, and the one category that's bucking the trend — bullpen_fatigue — is 0-1 in that same window riding a 5-game losing streak across the board. That's a real divergence worth noting: bullpen_fatigue has been the weak link all season (R1 at 47%, 520-598) and it's still cold right now, so any pick today where bullpen_fatigue is the lone category in disagreement should get discounted hard, while sp (riding 3-game win streaks at every rating tier) deserves extra weight when it lines up with trends or runs. The trends+sp combo remains the best agreement play in the data at 58.0% (370-268, n=638), and with trends hitting 56% at season scale (629-489, n=1118) across every rating, any game where trends and sp are both pointing the same direction is the sharpest angle on the board today.

On strong plays, R2 and R3 are the ratings to lean on — R2's 30-day window is 7-3 (70%, +3.0u) and R3 is 4-2 (67%) over the same span, both comfortably ahead of R1 and R4's flatter 30-day lines. If either of those ratings flags a strong play intersecting with MIL, TBR, BOS, or LAD today, take it seriously: those four teams are the model's best friends this season, with LAD strong plays hitting 80% (28-7, +27.0u) and BOS at 76% (22-7, +19.0u) — both elite conversion rates on the model's highest-conviction bets. Avoid leaning into NYY regardless of category agreement; the model is 49% overall on Yankees picks and strong plays have bled -4.0u (9-14), the only team in the top-volume group losing money on strong plays. If today's slate has LAD or BOS appearing as a strong play alongside trends+sp agreement, that's the shape of a top-tier card; if NYY shows up as a strong play, treat it as a fade candidate rather than a green light no matter what the rating says.
